data.summary: This 12‑week plan tackles the student’s weak units first, cycles through all units, and ends with a mixed review and timed practice. Each week is a single, focused session of 6 hours, with concrete tasks that can be completed in one sitting.

tasks: Read textbook sections on moles, atomic structure, and periodic trends.
Do 20 practice problems on mole calculations and electron configurations.
Create a flashcard set for key periodic trends.
Summarize mass spectroscopy principles.
Solve 15 problems on elemental composition of pure substances.
Watch a recorded lecture on photoelectron spectroscopy and take notes.
Diagram composition of mixtures.
Practice stoichiometry problems involving ionic compounds.
Write a short explanation of valence electrons in ionic bonding.
Create VSEPR models for 10 molecules.
Solve 10 problems on Lewis structures and hybridization.
Review bond types with flashcards.
Compare forces in solids, liquids, gases.
Do 15 practice questions on solid properties.
Draw phase diagrams for selected substances.
Derive Ideal Gas Law from kinetic theory.
Solve 20 problems on gas law applications.
Simulate gas behavior with an online tool.
Balance 15 reactions of various types.
Write net ionic equations for 10 reactions.
Calculate moles and mass in stoichiometry problems.
Plot concentration vs. time graphs for 5 reactions.
Determine rate laws from data sets.
Explain the relationship between rate constants and temperature.
Draw energy diagrams for 5 reactions.
Calculate heat changes using calorimetry data.
Solve 10 problems on heat capacity.
Compute equilibrium constants for 5 reactions.
Apply Le Chatelier’s principle to 10 scenarios.
Solve problems involving reaction quotients.
Calculate pH for 5 weak acid/base solutions.
Solve buffer capacity problems.
Derive Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.
Compute ΔG for 5 reactions.
Solve 10 problems on entropy changes.
Practice 5 galvanic cell calculations.
Take a 90‑minute timed practice test covering all units.
Review incorrect answers and update flashcards.
Plan a final review schedule for the week before the exam.

data.final_week_advice: In the final week, focus on full-length timed practice, identify remaining weak spots, and solidify concepts with quick review sessions. Ensure you’re comfortable with calculations, data interpretation, and concept explanations before the exam.
